clue.text: Restrained dog is suffering problems with some chow

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the three words before it have their letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog kept on a tight leash is having trouble with a chow or two.
explanation.walkthrough: Chow in the surface is the dog breed; in the definition it is slang for food. 'suffering' is the anagram signal for the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow is slang for food, so problems with it are conditions such as anorexia and bulimia.

clue.text: Relish English post, mostly in the big apple

indicators.note: in tells you the shortened word for post sits inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: the Big Apple is the nickname of New York, abbreviated NY

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for post is used

parts.note: a post is a job, a position of employment

explanation.surface: Savour a posting from England that is spent largely in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: To take great pleasure in something is to savour it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Pull to pieces what an unemployed actor hopes to do

definitions.meaning: to pull something to pieces is to dismantle it, or to criticise it harshly

definitions.text: what an unemployed actor hopes to do
definitions.meaning: an out-of-work actor wants to land a role in a play, a reading that splits the phrase into three words rather than two

explanation.surface: Savaging the ambitions of a performer who is out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismantling something is one sense; spaced differently, the phrase describes landing a stage role.

clue.text: Spy seen in new and old ship

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament
the ark was Noah's vessel in the Bible, about as old as ships get

explanation.surface: An agent is spotted aboard two vessels, one modern and one ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a police informer, who watches others and reports back in secret.

clue.text: Tired daughter showered

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter used in family trees
when it showered, it rained

explanation.surface: A weary girl took a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exhausted is said to be emptied of all energy, a common figurative synonym.

clue.text: Bags of pain in street ending in tears

indicators.note: in puts the word for pain inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street in addresses
an ache is a dull continuous pain

indicators.note: ending in asks for the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A great deal of suffering on one road finishes with crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags of' reads as 'lots of', but only the first word is the definition: small pouches, not plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small sealed pouches, for sugar or shampoo say, so little packets.

clue.text: Story-teller working near court

indicators.note: working here means operating on the two words after it, putting their letters in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teller of tales plies a trade close to the law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: From French, a person skilled at relating anecdotes entertainingly.

clue.text: Far right no longer show feeling

indicators.note: no longer says the letter for right, once present, is now gone from the word for far

parts.note: remote means far away

explanation.surface: Extreme right-wingers have stopped displaying any sentiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far right' reads as a political label, but the two words are separate: 'no longer' removes R from REMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To display one's sentiments openly, often theatrically, as an actor might.

clue.text: Mint on lamb, for example is a delicacy

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a mint is a kind of sweet, the British word for a piece of candy
lamb is one example of the flesh of an animal eaten as food

explanation.surface: Mint sauce served with roast lamb, say, makes a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a piece of confectionery or candied fruit, a dainty treat.

clue.text: Do you transport the lady speaking fast in eastern capital?

indicators.note: speaking fast says the phrase is said aloud and hurriedly, so its words run together

parts.note: do you cart her, said in a rush, comes out as 'd'you cart 'er'

explanation.surface: Asking a driver whether he carries a fast-talking woman around an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking fast' is the homophone signal. The slurred 'd'you cart 'er' needs a British accent that drops the R sounds and the H.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the chief city of Indonesia, in south-east Asia.

clue.text: Go by bike, carrying on in lots of wind

indicators.note: carrying means the word for going by bike holds the next word inside it

parts.note: to cycle is to travel by bicycle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pedal onwards through a blustery gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying on' reads as 'continuing', but the two words split: the first is the container signal and the second is what goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating storm, which brings a great deal of fast-moving air.

clue.text: Votes in favour of timeless Irish poet

indicators.note: timeless means lacking time, so the usual abbreviation for time is dropped from the poet's name

parts.note: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet who won the Nobel Prize in 1923
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Ballots backing an Irish poet whose work never dates.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliament, members supporting a motion call out this old word for yes.

clue.text: We hear one after another intended to get detention

indicators.note: we hear tells you the words that follow are listened to, not read

parts.note: things done one after another are done in turn; meant is the past tense of mean, to intend

explanation.surface: Word reaches us that pupil after pupil was meant to be kept in after school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' is the homophone signal: 'in turn meant' is what is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Confinement without trial, usually in wartime, so a form of being held.

clue.text: Progressive leader of Indian state

indicators.note: the leader of a place can be named place-first, so the state comes before the word for leader

parts.note: Goa is a small state on the west coast of India
the head of an organisation is its leader

explanation.surface: A forward-thinking chief minister in one part of India.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes an enterprising, forward-looking person or firm.

clue.text: Famous Russian composer in new edition of grove

indicators.note: in places the composer's name inside the rearranged letters
a new edition is a revised version, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
J. S. Bach was the German baroque composer

explanation.surface: A celebrated Russian musician appears in the latest Grove dictionary of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous Russian composer' wants to be the definition; only the first two words are. 'new edition of' gives GOREV, which 'in' then opens for the musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail, the last leader of the Soviet Union, known worldwide.

clue.text: Short-lived, wild maple here

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the two words after it run about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-seeded maple tree that will not last long in this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting only a very brief time, like a mayfly's adult life.

clue.text: Tower viewed in modified telescope company's put out

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters that remain are put in a new order
put out means ejected, so the letters for company leave the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A tall building is seen through an adapted telescope that its maker has issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes CO from TELESCOPE, leaving TELESPE, which 'modified' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's tall pointed structure, usually topped by a spire.

clue.text: Travelling pioneer keeping very quiet in what may be called a banger

definitions.text: what may be called a banger

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged word holds the musical marking inside it
travelling letters move about, so the word after it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
PP is pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A wandering trailblazer stays silent inside an old jalopy.
explanation.walkthrough: Banger is British slang for a sausage, and for an old car, which the surface suggests. 'Travelling' gives PEERONI before 'keeping' opens it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy Italian-American salami, so loosely one kind of sausage.

clue.text: Did gag that's despicable, wife walking out

indicators.note: walking out means leaving, so the letter for wife departs from the longer word

parts.note: a wretched act is a contemptible one
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogy

explanation.surface: A comedian told a vile joke and his wife left the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The gag looks like a joke; it is the heaving kind. 'walking out' removes W from WRETCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to heave as if about to vomit, here in the past tense.

clue.text: Scheduled to include one line over set boundaries

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the whole assembled string is read from its far end
to include means the word for scheduled takes the two short pieces inside it

parts.note: an event timed for noon is scheduled for noon
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for line, as in references to a text

explanation.surface: A timetable arranged to contain one extra route beyond the fixed limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts IL inside TIMED to give TIMILED, and 'over' turns that whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to fix the limits or extent of something, such as a territory.

clue.text: Railing about initially cutting standard brain scanning facility

indicators.note: cutting means the single letter slices in between the two pieces that follow

parts.note: par is the expected standard, as in 'below par'
PET is positron emission tomography, a scanning technique used on the brain

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Complaining at first about cuts to an ordinary hospital brain-scan unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railing about' reads as complaining, but Railing is a barrier and 'about' only lends its first letter, as 'initially' says, to the 'cutting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall or barrier along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Most classy lady's into cannabis

indicators.note: into means the letters for lady's go inside the word for cannabis

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
the lady is 'she', so lady's, short for 'lady is', gives she's

explanation.surface: The most upper-crust woman is keen on marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' reads as 'keen on', but here it is the container signal, and the possessive 's is really 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh is British informal for upper-class or stylish, here in the superlative.

clue.text: Finish sounding like a drunken side-kick!

indicators.note: the word is heard as a drunk would say it, with the final s sound slurred to sh

parts.note: an accomplice is a partner in crime, a side-kick

explanation.surface: End up resembling a tipsy assistant!
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding like a drunken' is a homophone with a twist: ACCOMPLICE is slurred, its last sound thickened to SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete a task successfully is to achieve or carry it out.

clue.text: Arrive before time in early jet

indicators.note: before puts the word for arrive ahead of the abbreviation for time

parts.note: to come is to arrive
T is the abbreviation for time in physics formulae

explanation.surface: Getting there ahead of schedule on a dawn flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early jet' looks like a morning flight; it is an aircraft from the early days of jet travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland airliner of 1952 was the world's first commercial passenger jet.

clue.text: Stages that go with 11 called out

definitions.meaning: the stages of a journey or a relay race are its separate sections
a British bingo caller announces the number 11 with this word before 'eleven', because the two digits look like a pair of limbs

explanation.surface: Sections of a rally that accompany number 11 being announced.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 is not a pointer to another clue: it is the number as a British bingo caller shouts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sections of a journey are one sense; the other is the word in the traditional bingo call for eleven.

clue.text: Do they help one to see what builders are doing?

definitions.text: Do they help one to see what builders are doing?

parts.words: Do they help one to see what builders are doing?
parts.note: glasses help one to see, and the same short word names the detailed written requirements that builders work from

explanation.definitionFit: Short for spectacles and for specifications, so both eyewear and a builder's working documents.

clue.text: Marries for one day?

definitions.meaning: a registrar or priest who marries a couple joins them in matrimony
'for one' and the question mark flag an example: this is a common short written form of the midweek day

explanation.surface: A wedding whose marriage lasts just twenty-four hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning joins in matrimony, and the usual abbreviation of Wednesday.

clue.text: Starts to hoover under machines, part of kitchen routine

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

parts.note: the kitchen is orchestral slang for the percussion section, where a drum belongs

explanation.surface: Begin vacuuming beneath the appliances as one of the regular household chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes the first letters of three words. 'Kitchen' is orchestral players' slang for the percussion section, so the household appliances are a blind.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, dull and monotonous, lacking any excitement or variety.

clue.text: Detective hurt and it doesn't look good

parts.note: an eye, short for private eye, is slang for a private detective
a sore knee is a hurt one

explanation.surface: A police investigator is injured and the outlook is bleak.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly that offends the sight, such as a derelict building.

clue.text: Important figures that are expanded by a corporation

definitions.text: Important figures that are expanded by a corporation

parts.words: Important figures that are expanded by a corporation
parts.note: figures are both numbers and body shapes, and a corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch, which increases a person's measurements

explanation.surface: Key numbers that a big company has inflated.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a person's bust, waist and hip measurements, which a large belly would enlarge; literally essential numerical data.
